$comment: Settings for an UNATTENDED run. Loaded with --settings, and deliberately NARROWER than the interactive profile — an unattended agent gets fewer capabilities, never more.
$never: Do not add --bare to the launch command. Bare mode skips hooks, which removes the Stop gate that
is the entire basis for 'the agent cannot claim success', and it also bypasses stored credentials
so the run silently bills per token instead of using the subscription.
Do not use --permission-mode bypassPermissions or --dangerously-skip-permissions. Those permit
writes to protected paths, so the agent could delete the very guardrails meant to contain it.
Use dontAsk: it denies anything not explicitly allowed, never waits for input, and — critically —
denies the ask-a-question tool, so the only way out is finishing or writing BLOCKED.md.

$denyNotes.dependencies: A new dependency is the highest-consequence thing an unattended run can add, and the thing a prompt-injected agent would most want to add. A spec that needs an unforeseen library ends BLOCKED — that costs one morning decision.
$denyNotes.push-and-gh: The run itself cannot push or use gh. Reaching the default branch happens only through merge-run.sh, which re-verifies everything and requires autonomy.mayMerge. With mayMerge off (the default) the run produces a local branch and stops.
$denyNotes.self-modification: Guardrails, gate scripts and the project declaration are off limits. An agent that can edit its own gates has no gates.
$denyNotes.main: The run works on its own branch. It must not be able to switch to or reset the default branch.

$allowNotes.merge-run: The ONLY route to the default branch. Ad-hoc `git push origin main` stays denied and stays blocked by the guard. This script re-runs the gates and the coverage check on the branch, requires the risk classifier to return 'auto', and re-checks the gates AFTER merging — because a clean merge of two green branches can still be broken. Enabled per project by autonomy.mayMerge.
